events.summary: TSM fell 2.09% to $472.20 on Wednesday after -0.72% on Tuesday (-2.80% over two days from Monday's record close). About two-fifths of Wednesday's drop came from chip stocks as a group (SMH -1.18%); TSMC's own part (-1.12 points, z -0.83) was smaller than one normal company-specific day (1.36 points). US stocks slipped from Tuesday's records as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.31% and investors waited for the Fed's September meeting minutes (2 p.m. ET); markets priced about a 20% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike later in October. TipRanks says TSM's dip was due to the yield rise and the Fed minutes, not company news.
events.why_it_matters: No company news explains the drop; it is a normal-size pullback driven by rates and the chip sector after a record high. It does not touch any thesis pillar.

events.summary: Citi (analyst Laura Chen) raised its target for the Taipei-listed shares to NT$4,000 from NT$3,800 and kept Buy. Citi's Atif Malik expects TSMC to beat its own Q3 guidance (Citi opened a 90-day 'catalyst watch'), more than 40% year-over-year revenue growth into 2027, and AI revenue nearly doubling next year, citing AI computing demand, agentic AI and co-packaged optics. Quote (Malik): 'Supported by robust AI compute demand, potential upside from agentic AI, and the new networking cycle of CPO, we expect >40% year over year revenue growth for TSMC into 2027E.'
events.why_it_matters: Opinion, not fact. It shows the bar for Q3 is high: a respected analyst is publicly expecting a beat. The stock fell on the same day, so the note did not drive the price.

events.summary: AMD CEO Lisa Su, on her third Taiwan visit of the year, said AMD will raise its Taiwan supply-chain investment beyond the US$10 billion announced in May ('We're increasing that number going forward because our demand has continued to go up'; new amount not given). She said demand for CPUs, GPUs and AI products exceeds supply ('we can definitely use more'), that AMD is extending planning with partners including TSMC from 1-2 years to 3-5 years, plans to 'substantially increase' supply in 2027, and was going to Hsinchu to meet TSMC.

why_chain.text: TSM closed $472.20 on Wed 2026-10-07 (-2.09%) after -0.72% on Tuesday: -2.80% in two days from Monday's record close of $485.80.

Neither day was unusual for TSMC itself: the company-specific part was -0.79 points on Tuesday (z -0.58) and -1.12 on Wednesday (z -0.83), both smaller than one typical company move (1.36 points). Chip stocks as a group pulled it down: industry part -0.57 Tue and -0.70 Wed; SMH -1.18% Wed.

On Wednesday US stocks retreated from Tuesday's record highs as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.31% and investors waited for the Fed's September-meeting minutes (2 p.m. ET). TipRanks attributes TSM's dip to the same thing, not to company news.

Markets are debating whether the Fed will RAISE rates: weak September US payrolls (+29,000 vs 84,000 expected) cut the priced odds of a hike from 64.2% to 22.7% on Monday, and on Wednesday markets priced about a 20% chance of a 25-basis-point hike later in October.

Basic driver: higher interest rates make profits expected years from now worth less today, so richly valued growth stocks such as chipmakers fall most when yields rise. TSM trades at about 30 times past earnings, above its 5-year median of about 22.6 (GuruFocus).
The small company-specific remainder may be profit-taking after a record high (RSI 72.6) and ahead of Thursday's September sales report; no source says so and no negative TSMC news was found.

products.name: Leading-edge wafer manufacturing (3-nanometre and 2-nanometre processes) for AI and computer chips
products.what_it_is: TSMC's newest chip-making processes, used to make the AI processors and CPUs that customers such as AMD and NVIDIA design.
products.analogy: A printing house whose newest presses print far more detail per page; designers pay more to use them because their books (chips) come out faster and use less power.
products.buyers: Chip designers: AMD (Lisa Su said on 2026-10-06 its demand exceeds supply and it is planning 3-5 years ahead with TSMC), NVIDIA, Apple, Broadcom and others.
products.how_it_works: TSMC etches billions of transistors onto silicon wafers; smaller 'nanometre' generations fit more transistors per chip. Customers buy finished wafers; TSMC then often packages several chips together (advanced packaging) for AI processors.
products.price: Not disclosed by TSMC. Unconfirmed press reports of 5-10% price rises on advanced processes (TrendForce 2026-10-05, already in the news log).
products.sales: Q2 2026: 3nm 30%, 5nm 33%, 2nm 3%, 7nm 11% of wafer revenue; 7nm and more advanced = 77% of wafer revenue. Total Q2 revenue US$40.20bn.
products.stage: 3nm in high-volume production; 2nm ramping (3% of Q2 wafer revenue).
products.size_for_company: Advanced processes are about three-quarters of wafer revenue (77% in Q2 2026).
products.competition: Samsung Foundry and Intel Foundry offer competing advanced processes; neither has been confirmed to have won a top customer's leading AI chip in volume in this window.
products.why_investors_care: These processes earn TSMC's highest margins; AMD's comment that demand exceeds supply into 2027 points to continued full factories.
products.watch_next: Q3 results 2026-10-15: share of revenue from 2nm and 3nm, and how much 2nm costs weigh on the gross margin (guided 65-67%).
